ei.title: Why Two Reasons Are Worse Than One
ei.subject: 올림포스전국연합고1_2026

fullPassage: My colleagues and I ran an experiment testing two different messages meant to convince thousands of resistant alumni to make a donation. One message emphasized the opportunity to do good: donating would benefit students, faculty, and staff. The other emphasized the opportunity to feel good: donors would enjoy the warm glow of giving. The two messages were equally effective: in both cases, 6.5 percent of the unwilling alumni ended up donating. Then we combined them, because two reasons are better than one. Except they weren't. When we put the two reasons together, the giving rate dropped below 3 percent. Each reason alone was more than twice as effective as the two combined. The audience was already skeptical. When we gave them different kinds of reasons to donate, we triggered their awareness that someone was trying to persuade them — and they shielded themselves against it.

questions.passage: My colleagues and I ran an experiment testing two different messages meant to (A)[convince / discourage] thousands of resistant alumni to make a donation. One message emphasized the opportunity to do good: donating would benefit students, faculty, and staff. The other emphasized the opportunity to feel good: donors would enjoy the warm glow of giving. The two messages were equally (B)[useless / effective]: in both cases, 6.5 percent of the unwilling alumni ended up donating. Then we (C)[combined / separated] them, because two reasons are better than one. Except they weren't. When we put the two reasons together, the giving rate dropped below 3 percent. Each reason alone was more than twice as effective as the two combined. The audience was already skeptical. When we gave them different kinds of reasons to donate, we triggered their awareness that someone was trying to persuade them — and they shielded themselves against it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: ① (A) convince(설득하다) (B) effective(효과적인) (C) combined(결합했다) 원문 그대로
det.analysis:
✅ ① convince(설득하다)+effective(효과적인)+combined(결합했다) ← 정답
❌ ② discourage(단념시키다) ≠ convince
❌ ③ useless(쓸모없는) ≠ effective, separated(분리했다) ≠ combined
❌ ④ discourage+useless = 2개 오류

questions.passage: My colleagues and I ran an experiment testing two different messages meant to convince thousands of resistant alumni to make a donation. One message (A)[emphasized / hid] the opportunity to do good: donating would (B)[harm / benefit] students, faculty, and staff. The other emphasized the opportunity to feel good: donors would enjoy the warm glow of giving. The two messages were equally effective: in both cases, 6.5 percent of the unwilling alumni ended up donating. Then we combined them, because two reasons are better than one. Except they weren't. When we put the two reasons together, the giving rate (C)[dropped / rose] below 3 percent. Each reason alone was more than twice as effective as the two combined. The audience was already skeptical. When we gave them different kinds of reasons to donate, we triggered their awareness that someone was trying to persuade them — and they shielded themselves against it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: ② (A) emphasized(강조했다) (B) benefit(이익을 주다) (C) dropped(떨어졌다) 원문 그대로
det.analysis:
❌ ① hid(숨겼다) ≠ emphasized
✅ ② emphasized(강조했다)+benefit(이익을 주다)+dropped(떨어졌다) ← 정답
❌ ③ harm(해를 끼치다) ≠ benefit, rose(올랐다) ≠ dropped
❌ ④ hid+harm = 2개 오류

questions.passage: My colleagues and I ran an experiment testing two different messages meant to convince thousands of (A)[resistant / eager] alumni to make a donation. One message emphasized the opportunity to do good: donating would benefit students, faculty, and staff. The other emphasized the opportunity to feel good: donors would enjoy the warm glow of giving. The two messages were equally effective: in both cases, 6.5 percent of the unwilling alumni ended up donating. Then we combined them, because two reasons are better than one. Except they weren't. When we put the two reasons together, the giving rate dropped below 3 percent. Each reason alone was more than twice as effective as the two combined. The audience was already (B)[trusting / skeptical]. When we gave them different kinds of reasons to donate, we triggered their awareness that someone was trying to persuade them — and they (C)[shielded / exposed] themselves against it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: ④ (A) resistant(저항하는) (B) skeptical(회의적인) (C) shielded(보호했다) 원문 그대로
det.analysis:
❌ ① eager(열망하는) ≠ resistant
❌ ② trusting(신뢰하는) ≠ skeptical, exposed(노출시켰다) ≠ shielded
❌ ③ eager+trusting+exposed = 3개 오류
✅ ④ resistant(저항하는)+skeptical(회의적인)+shielded(보호했다) ← 정답

questions.passage: My colleagues and I ran an experiment testing two different messages meant to ①<u>convince</u> thousands of resistant alumni to make a donation. One message emphasized the opportunity to do good: donating would benefit students, faculty, and staff. The other emphasized the opportunity to feel good: donors would enjoy the warm glow of giving. The two messages were ②<u>equally ineffective</u>: in both cases, 6.5 percent of the unwilling alumni ended up donating. Then we ③<u>combined</u> them, because two reasons are better than one. Except they weren't. When we put the two reasons together, the giving rate ④<u>dropped</u> below 3 percent. Each reason alone was more than twice as effective as the two combined. The audience was already skeptical. When we gave them different kinds of reasons to donate, we triggered their awareness that someone was trying to persuade them — and they shielded themselves against it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② equally ineffective → equally effective: 두 메시지는 똑같이 '효과적'이었다
det.analysis:
✅ ① convince: 설득하다, 적절
❌ ② equally ineffective → equally effective: 두 메시지 모두 6.5%가 기부했으므로 똑같이 효과적(effective)이었다. ineffective(효과 없는)는 반대 ← 정답
✅ ③ combined: 결합했다, 적절
✅ ④ dropped: 떨어졌다, 적절

questions.passage: My colleagues and I ran an experiment testing two different messages meant to convince thousands of resistant alumni to make a donation. The other emphasized the opportunity to feel good: donors would enjoy the warm glow of giving. The two messages were equally effective: in both cases, 6.5 percent of the unwilling alumni ended up donating. Then we combined them, because two reasons are better than one. Except they weren't. When we put the two reasons together, the giving rate ③<u>rose</u> below 3 percent. Each reason alone was more than twice as effective as the two combined. The audience was already ④<u>skeptical</u>. When we gave them different kinds of reasons to donate, we triggered their awareness that someone was trying to persuade them — and they shielded themselves against it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ rose → dropped: 두 이유를 합치자 기부율이 '떨어졌다'
det.analysis:
✅ ① emphasized: 강조했다, 적절
✅ ② benefit: 이익을 주다, 적절
❌ ③ rose → dropped: 두 이유를 합쳤을 때 기부율이 3% 아래로 떨어졌다(dropped). rose(올랐다)는 반대 ← 정답
✅ ④ skeptical: 회의적인, 적절
det.tip: the giving rate dropped = 기부율이 떨어졌다 ↔ rose
